diff --git a/scripts/hive-common.sh b/scripts/hive-common.sh
index f71c43c..73b52d3 100755
--- a/scripts/hive-common.sh
+++ b/scripts/hive-common.sh
@@ -55,6 +55,112 @@ OPERATOR_ACTOR="operator"
 
 die() { echo "hive: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
 
+# --- the shared Predictions parser (one parser, two callers) -------------------
+# R2/D1: hive-score parses bullet LABELS while the launch gate used to be a human
+# reading a HEADING, so the whole tenant project's first wave scored unpredicted
+# with no error anywhere (retro 2026-07-29 D1). The repair is a single parser in
+# hive-common.sh, called by hive-score (to record coverage) and by hive-launch (to
+# refuse an unparseable section before any spine write). A gate that calls the
+# same functions the scorer uses cannot drift into a second dialect.
+#
+# `- Named risks:` is required by the authoring protocol and written by every
+# author, and read by no instrument: it is REPORTED (it is one of the four literal
+# labels printed by a refusal) but never COUNTED among the three scored fields.
+# Scoring it would be a gate-content change, which is the operator's call, not a
+# worker's (retro 2026-07-29 R9, held).
+# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # PRED_LABELS is consumed by hive-launch's refusal (sourced caller)
+PRED_LABELS=( "Expected effort:" "Expected questions:" "Expected review outcome:" "Named risks:" )
+
+# parse_predictions <order-file>  — set the PRED_* globals below.
+# The single source of truth for an order's `## Predictions` section (from that
+# heading to the next heading of any level, exclusive). Works on the file's text
+# only — it never writes to the file (stop-line: tooling never edits an order).
+# Sets:
+#   PRED_HAS_SECTION  "1" / ""    a `## Predictions` heading was found
+#   PRED_DECLARED     "1" / ""    the section carries the protocol's one-line
+#                                 declared-unpredicted disposition
+#   PRED_SECTION                  the raw section text ("" when absent)
+#   PRED_EFFORT_TXT               verbatim value after `Expected effort:`
+#   PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT            verbatim value after `Expected questions:`
+#   PRED_REVIEW_TXT               verbatim value after `Expected review outcome:`
+#   PRED_FIELDS                   0..3 how many of the three scored fields parsed
+#   PRED_MISSING                  comma-separated literal labels (among the three
+#                                 scored) that did NOT parse ("" when all parsed)
+#   PRED_OFFENDING                the section's lines that parsed to no scored
+#                                 field and are not the declared-unpredicted line
+#                                 (newline-separated; for the launch refusal)
+parse_predictions() {  # parse_predictions <order-file>
+  local f="$1"
+  PRED_HAS_SECTION=""; PRED_DECLARED=""; PRED_SECTION=""
+  PRED_EFFORT_TXT=""; PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT=""; PRED_REVIEW_TXT=""
+  PRED_FIELDS=0; PRED_MISSING=""; PRED_OFFENDING=""
+  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
+
+  PRED_SECTION=$(awk '
+    /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { inblock = 1; next }
+    inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }
+    inblock                        { print }
+  ' "$f")
+  [ -n "$PRED_SECTION" ] || return 0
+  PRED_HAS_SECTION=1
+
+  # The protocol's one-line declared-unpredicted disposition: "one line declaring
+  # the task deliberately unpredicted and why". A declared-unpredicted section is
+  # a recorded metric, never a launch error (stop-line: refusal is on unparseable,
+  # never on absent).
+  if printf '%s\n' "$PRED_SECTION" | grep -qiE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*[Dd]eclared[[:space:]]+[Uu]npredicted:'; then
+    PRED_DECLARED=1
+  fi
+
+  # The three scored fields. The regexes are the whole parse: `hive-score` and the
+  # launch gate agree on these byte for byte because both call this function.
+  PRED_EFFORT_TXT=$( { printf '%s\n' "$PRED_SECTION" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected effort:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.–—-]*[[:space:]]*worker-hours?' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected effort:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+  PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT=$( { printf '%s\n' "$PRED_SECTION" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected questions:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9–—-]*' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected questions:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+  PRED_REVIEW_TXT=$( { printf '%s\n' "$PRED_SECTION" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected review outcome:[[:space:]]*[^.]+' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected review outcome:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+
+  local -a miss=()
+  [ -n "$PRED_EFFORT_TXT" ]    || miss+=( "Expected effort" )
+  [ -n "$PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT" ] || miss+=( "Expected questions" )
+  [ -n "$PRED_REVIEW_TXT" ]    || miss+=( "Expected review outcome" )
+  PRED_FIELDS=$(( 3 - ${#miss[@]} ))
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # PRED_MISSING is consumed by hive-score / hive-launch (sourced callers)
+  PRED_MISSING=$(IFS=,; printf '%s' "${miss[*]}")
+
+  # The lines that parsed to no scored field and are not the declared-unpredicted
+  # line — what a launch refusal prints so the operator can see the dialect.
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # PRED_OFFENDING is consumed by hive-launch's refusal (sourced caller)
+  PRED_OFFENDING=$( { printf '%s\n' "$PRED_SECTION" \
+    | grep -viE 'Expected effort:|Expected questions:|Expected review outcome:' \
+    | grep -viE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*[Dd]eclared[[:space:]]+[Uu]npredicted:' \
+    | sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d'; } || true )
+}
+
+# assess_predictions <order-file>  — prints "refuse", "warn", or "allow".
+# The launch gate's teeth (R2): a `## Predictions` section that is present,
+# carries no declared-unpredicted disposition, and parses NONE of the three
+# scored fields refuses the launch before any spine write; --anyway is the escape
+# hatch. A partial section (1-2 of 3) warns loudly and launches. An absent
+# section and a declared-unpredicted section both allow (the gap and the
+# declaration are recorded metrics, not errors).
+assess_predictions() {  # assess_predictions <order-file>
+  parse_predictions "$1"
+  if [ -z "$PRED_HAS_SECTION" ] || [ -n "$PRED_DECLARED" ]; then
+    printf 'allow'
+  elif [ "$PRED_FIELDS" -eq 0 ]; then
+    printf 'refuse'
+  elif [ "$PRED_FIELDS" -lt 3 ]; then
+    printf 'warn'
+  else
+    printf 'allow'
+  fi
+}
+
 # Refuse a tmux session name that cannot be targeted safely. Task, worker and run
 # ids are all charset-guarded because they flow into tmux targets and generated
 # shell; HIVE_TMUX_SESSION flows into the very same targets and was not — and a
@@ -217,9 +323,15 @@ order_pin() {  # order_pin <workspace-relative-path>  -> prints sha

-# retry (push -> pull --rebase -> push) and reports precisely how far it got, so
-# "committed locally" is never mistaken for "on the hub".
+# spine prefix legitimately produces no diff.
+#
+# A push failure REFUSES rather than rebasing (retro 2 ledger 13, Watch folded by
+# instrument-teeth scope 6): commit_metrics is now reached automatically on EVERY
+# close and instrument refresh, so an unattended `pull --rebase` on a shared
+# metrics path is how a conflicting entry silently wins. The commit stays local,
+# the manual resolution step is printed, and the caller reports non-zero — the
+# report says precisely how far it got, so "committed locally" is never mistaken
+# for "on the hub".

   local msg="$2" spec="projects/$1/metrics"
   git -C "$OPS_WS" add -- "$spec" || { echo "hive: git add failed for $spec in $OPS_WS" >&2; return 1; }
@@ -230,12 +342,12 @@ commit_metrics() {  # commit_metrics <project> <commit-message>  -> 0 committed/
   git -C "$OPS_WS" commit --quiet -m "$msg" -- "$spec" \
     || { echo "hive: git commit failed for $spec in $OPS_WS (git identity unset, a commit hook, or an index lock?)" >&2; return 1; }
   if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
-    if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" pull --rebase --quiet; then
-      echo "hive: push failed and rebase failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, NOT on the hub; resolve by hand" >&2
-      return 1
-    fi
-    git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet \
-      || { echo "hive: push failed for $OPS_WS — committed locally, NOT on the hub" >&2; return 1; }
+    {
+      echo "hive: push failed for $OPS_WS — $spec is committed LOCALLY, NOT on the hub."
+      echo "hive: refusing to auto-rebase a shared metrics path (the improver reads only what is on the hub)."
+      echo "hive: resolve by hand: git -C $OPS_WS pull --rebase && git -C $OPS_WS push"
+    } >&2
+    return 1
   fi
   echo "  committed + pushed: $spec ($msg)"
 }

+## What shipped
+

+drill-hygiene fold is the two named classes only.

+- **`scripts/hive-common.sh`** — the shared Predictions parser, factored here as the single
+  source of truth for an order's `## Predictions` section:
+  - `parse_predictions <order-file>` sets `PRED_HAS_SECTION` / `PRED_DECLARED` / `PRED_FIELDS` /
+    `PRED_MISSING` / `PRED_OFFENDING` / the three `*_TXT` verbatim values. It reads the file's
+    text only; it never writes to the order (stop-line: tooling never edits an order body).
+  - `assess_predictions <order-file>` prints `refuse` | `warn` | `allow` — the gate's teeth.
+  - `PRED_LABELS` — the four literal bullet labels, printed by a refusal. `Named risks:` is
+    **reported** (printed) but never **counted** among the three scored fields (R9 held; a
+    gate-content change is the operator's call, not a worker's).
+  - `commit_metrics` **refuses rather than rebases** on push failure (scope 6): the commit stays
+    local, the manual resolution step is printed (`git pull --rebase && git push`), and the caller
+    returns non-zero. The old `push → pull --rebase → push` retry is gone.
+- **`scripts/hive-launch`** — the predictions gate (scope 1 + 2). Before any spine write, the
+  launch calls `assess_predictions` on the pinned order. A `## Predictions` section that is
+  present, carries no declared-unpredicted line, and parses none of the three scored fields
+  **refuses** — the message names the four literal labels, prints the offending lines, and names
+  `--anyway` as the deliberate escape. An absent section and the declared-unpredicted one-liner
+  launch cleanly; a 1–2-of-3 partial warns loudly and launches. Same parser `hive-score` uses.

+## Reflection
+
+- **The prose half failed exactly as D1 predicted, and the code half now cannot.** The
+  `- **Effort:**` dialect order `projects/pln-benchmarks/orders/2026-07-29-pw-writeup.md` was
+  caught at the wave-3 cut by a human doing the same reading that failed in wave 2. This order
+  makes that reading a launch gate with its own escape hatch, so the next author who re-words a
+  label gets a refusal that names the literal labels and prints the offending lines — not a
+  quiet `unpredicted` at scoring time. The gate is deliberately narrower than "has a Predictions
+  heading": absent and declared-unpredicted sections are recorded metrics, not errors, and the
+  refusal is on unparseable only.
+- **One parser, proven rather than asserted.** The reviewer's question for scope 2 was whether
+  the launch gate and the scorer are one parser or two that currently agree. The drill answers it
+  with a single input (`theta`) driven through both callers: the gate refuses it, the scorer
+  records it as section-present-unparsed. There is one regex set in the codebase and it lives in
+  `hive-common.sh`.
+- **`Named risks:` stayed unscored and got documented instead.** The order inherited R2's "N of 4"
+  vs the instrument's "3 scored fields" correction; the parser prints `Named risks:` among the
+  four literal labels but never counts it. That distinction is now in the code comment, the
+  launch-refusal message, and the RUNBOOK.
+- **Drill-hygiene sweep (DoD h), by class:**
+  - **Class 1 — EXIT-trap-before-isolation ordering.** `hive-metrics-drill.sh`: **none found** —
+    the drill is hermetic (no tmux, no live stack), its only cleanup is `rm -rf $SANDBOX`, which
+    has no default-socket hazard, so there is no isolation primitive whose ordering could bite.
+    `hive-tooling-drill.sh` already carries the fix (tmux isolation precedes the trap).
+  - **Class 2 — `cmd | grep -q` SIGPIPE under `set -o pipefail`.** `hive-metrics-drill.sh`:
+    **22 instances fixed** — every `grep -q*` at the right end of a pipeline changed to
+    `grep ... >/dev/null`, so a match no longer SIGPIPEs the producer (the passing case is
+    exactly when `-q` exits early). No rewrite, no restructure, no new framework — the fixes are
+    the one-token kind the order's bound allows. The remaining `grep -q` calls in the file are
+    direct file greps (not pipelines) and are unaffected.
+  - **No third class was found.** The boundary the order set ("a third defect class found is a
+    finding for the report, not a scope expansion") did not fire.
+- **A coverage string changed by the order's own wording.** `hive-score` previously recorded
+  `unpredicted (no usable \`## Predictions\` section)`; the order specifies
+  `unpredicted (no \`## Predictions\` section)`. The word "usable" is gone, and the two distinct
+  strings now match the order byte for byte.
+- **`--review` validation closes a real wave-2 column.** Retro 1's instrument note said lowercase
+  only, but wave 2 produced `Rework`, `Clean`, and `minor rework` into the same column. The
+  validator is three literal values, case-insensitive, stored lowercase — the column can no
+  longer drift back.
+- **The close→metrics coupling's blast radius is contained, twice.** The score-failure case
+  (already drilled) and the metrics-failure case (new) both prove the same discipline: the close
+  emits first, the follow-ups are non-fatal, and a broken remote leaves a loud complaint naming
+  exactly one recovery command. That the metrics step was added at all raises `commit_metrics`
+  firing rate — which is precisely why scope 6 (refuse, never rebase) rode in the same PR.
